pharm: High-potency phenothiazine antipsychotic; dopamine D2 receptor antagonist available as short-acting HCl and long-acting decanoate depot.
quick: Decanoate: 12.5-25 mg IM/SC initially, every 2-4 weeks; HCl 2.5-10 mg/day PO divided
Oral may be taken with or without food
Use only if clearly needed; neonatal EPS/withdrawal in 3rd trimester
Excreted in milk; weigh risk/benefit, generally avoid
Use with caution; no specific protocol
EPS/tardive dyskinesia, CBC, LFTs, metabolic, ECG
summary: Fluphenazine is a high-potency phenothiazine (typical) antipsychotic for schizophrenia. The decanoate is a long-acting depot injection for patients needing prolonged parenteral therapy. It carries a boxed warning for increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (not an approved use). High-potency dopamine blockade gives a substantial risk of extrapyramidal symptoms and tardive dyskinesia, plus risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome. It is contraindicated in liver damage, blood dyscrasias, comatose/severely depressed states, and subcortical brain damage.
indications: Management of schizophrenia and psychotic disorders
Long-acting maintenance (decanoate) for patients requiring prolonged parenteral antipsychotic therapy, e.g., chronic schizophrenia

dosage.n: Maintenance often 1-5 mg/day once daily; max ~40 mg/day
Onset 24-72 h; effect on psychosis significant within 48-96 h
A single injection may control symptoms up to 4 weeks or more

dosage.d: Approx 12.5 mg decanoate per ~10 mg/day oral HCl
dosage.n: Establish response to short-acting form before using decanoate in phenothiazine-naive patients

admin: Decanoate: deep IM or SC injection using a dry syringe and needle of at least 21 gauge (a wet needle clouds the solution)
Determine the patient's tolerance to fluphenazine with a short-acting form before starting the long-acting decanoate
Adjust subsequent decanoate dose and interval according to response
Oral forms may be given with or without food
moa: Postsynaptic dopamine D2 receptor antagonism in mesolimbic pathways reduces positive psychotic symptoms; the phenothiazine also blocks other receptors (alpha-adrenergic, muscarinic, histaminergic), accounting for adverse effects. The decanoate ester provides slow release from the injection depot.

absolute: Suspected or established subcortical brain damage

preg: Use only if clearly needed; neonates exposed in the third trimester are at risk of extrapyramidal and/or withdrawal symptoms after delivery. Monitor newborns.
lact: Phenothiazines are excreted in breast milk; potential for adverse effects in the infant. Generally avoid or weigh risk against benefit.
renal: Use with caution; no specific dosing protocol established. Monitor for accumulation of effects.
hepatic: Contraindicated in the presence of liver damage; phenothiazines are hepatically metabolized and can cause cholestatic injury.

major: CNS depressants (alcohol, opioids, benzodiazepines, anesthetics) - additive sedation/respiratory depression
moderate: Anticholinergics - additive antimuscarinic effects, may worsen tardive dyskinesia
interactions.food: Oral may be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: Avoid - additive CNS depression and orthostasis
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive pregnancy/PKU tests; can alter ECG (QT).

common: Anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, urinary retention)
emergency: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (hyperthermia, rigidity, autonomic instability)

monitoring: Extrapyramidal symptoms and abnormal involuntary movements (AIMS for tardive dyskinesia)
counsel: Take/receive exactly as prescribed; the depot injection works over weeks
Report muscle stiffness, tremor, restlessness, or uncontrolled movements
Seek urgent care for high fever with muscle rigidity and confusion
Rise slowly to avoid dizziness; avoid alcohol
Use sun protection (photosensitivity); report sore throat, fever, or yellowing of skin
pk: Decanoate ~2-4 weeks (up to 6 weeks in some)
Protect from light; store at controlled room temperature; do not freeze injection
pearls: Boxed warning: increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis - not approved for that use
High-potency phenothiazine - prominent extrapyramidal symptoms and tardive dyskinesia risk; relatively less sedation/hypotension than low-potency agents
Establish tolerance with short-acting fluphenazine before committing to the long-acting decanoate
Contraindicated with liver damage, blood dyscrasia, and comatose/severely depressed states
missed: For depot injections, give the missed dose as soon as feasible and adjust the schedule per clinician. For oral therapy, take the missed dose when remembered unless near the next dose; do not double up. Abrupt discontinuation may cause withdrawal/dyskinesia.
overdose: Overdose causes CNS depression, hypotension, severe extrapyramidal reactions, agitation, seizures, hyperthermia, and arrhythmias. No specific antidote. Provide supportive care, airway/respiratory and cardiovascular support, and ECG monitoring; treat dystonia with anticholinergics (e.g., benztropine, diphenhydramine), hypotension with IV fluids and pressors (avoid epinephrine), and arrhythmias appropriately. Dialysis is not helpful.
